Takarada and colleagues (265) demonstrated that although markers of muscle damage were attenuated after BFR training, there was evidence of fine microdamage within myofibers, leaving open the possibility that damage may have contributed to the results. Moreover, it remains possible that hypertrophy would have been enhanced to an even greater extent had EIMD been heightened in the BFR group. Markers of muscle damage following BFR have been demonstrated elsewhere, including lengthy decrements in maximal voluntary contraction, heightened delayed-onset muscle soreness, and elevated sarcolemmal permeability (64, 298, 299).
